Fix false "Could not reach PyPI" update check + tighten instance-lock PID match

PyPI update check: the /pypi/<pkg>/json metadata blob grows ~6 KB per
release and crossed the 256 KB response cap (~257 KB at v1.0.36), so
_fetch_latest_pypi_version rejected every real response as oversized and
returned None -> "Could not reach PyPI" (the `update` CLI and the in-app
update notice) while PyPI was perfectly reachable. Raise the cap to 8 MiB
and log a distinct warning on a genuinely oversized response. +3 tests.

_pid_is_splicecraft: matched "splicecraft" as a bare substring anywhere in
a process's cmdline, so any process whose path merely contained it (the
pipx venv at .../venvs/splicecraft/, a dev tree at ~/SpliceCraft/, an
editor on splicecraft.py) registered as a live instance -> spurious
"another instance is already running" lock-out when the recorded PID was
recycled. Match the splicecraft command/script token by basename instead
(still detects console-script, `python splicecraft.py`, `-m`, and pipx
launches, so a live lock is never freed). +2 tests.

Fix CI: scrub lone surrogates from log records (pytest-xdist 9.1)

The Tests workflow INTERNALERRORed on test_log_event_with_surrogate_does_not_raise:
pytest 9.1 serialises the captured LogRecord across the xdist worker boundary and
execnet cannot UTF-8-encode a lone surrogate, crashing the whole run. (CI installs
pytest>=9.0.3 → 9.1; local devs on the 9.0.3 floor never saw it.) New
_SurrogateScrubFilter on the splicecraft logger backslash-escapes surrogates on
every record before any handler or test-capture sees them. Verified against a
clean pytest-9.1 env that reproduced the crash.

Path dispatch is unchanged (the if/elif still keys on the file path; only the call is routed through the hook, guarded is-not-None for the import window where no save runs). Behavior-preserving by construction — proven before any code moves.

refactor(phase B-main/3): extract the persistence engine into splicecraft_persistence

The domain-agnostic save/load ENGINE — 28 top-level units, ~1525 lines — moves out of the hub into a new layer-1 sibling: _safe_save_json (atomic .bak+mkstemp+fsync+os.replace, read-back validation, shrink guard, lost-entries spillover), _safe_load_json (backup recovery + schema migrate), _atomic_write_{text,bytes}, the backup rotation/prune/compress helpers, _extract_entries/_migrate_entries (+ the empty _ENTRY_MIGRATIONS registry), and the _refuse_unauthorized_{write,delete} chokepoint enforcement.

The sibling imports ONLY stdlib + splicecraft_state + splicecraft_logging — never the hub. Everything it needs from the hub was already decoupled: paths/caches/flags/tunables read as _state.X (Phases A + B-main/1), blob dehydration via _state._dehydrate_*_hook (B-main/2), and the chokepoint reads _state._SAVES_AUTHORIZED (A2c). The domain _save_X/_load_X wrappers + the _authorize_writes* policy + the blob store stay hub-side and call the engine; they migrate with their domains later. Fix the public-surface CI failure on Python 3.12 (3.14-only module dunders)

The "Tests" CI job has failed on every release since v1.0.85 (modularization
start) while Publish/Docs stayed green: test_public_surface.py::

3.14 puts in `dir(<module>)` but 3.12 does NOT. The baseline was (re)snapshotted on

They are interpreter internals, never SpliceCraft's public API — not a real surface
regression, so the package kept publishing fine.

Fix: scrub both dunders from public_surface_baseline.json AND exclude a
_VERSION_SPECIFIC_DUNDERS set from the comparison on both ends, so the surface
test is interpreter-stable — a baseline regenerated on 3.14 can no longer break
the 3.12 CI (or vice-versa). test_public_surface 3 passed on 3.14; the baseline no
longer references either 3.14-only name, so 3.12 passes too.
